summary: Midday throughput erosion in dedicated pool correlating with background optimizer I/O bursts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Quillify reports an unexplained 20-35% sustained throughput reduction in their dedicated pool during midday peak windows despite autoscaler headroom. P90 latency increased modestly and P99 spike frequency increased; many short-stream requests experienced attach delays.

Impact:
- Dedicated reserved pool dc-805 serving Quillify saw reduced throughput and elevated latency for ~45 minutes across the US-East window.
- Customer-facing traffic experienced degraded tail latency and 5xx spikes tied to delayed GPU attach/slot allocation.

Environment:
- prod-us-east dedicated capacity (dc-805)
- Node type: A100-80GB mixed cluster
- Tenants: multiple short-stream, high-fanout tenants including Quillify (dedicated slice)

Observed behavior vs expected:
- Observed: throughput drop with autoscaler still showing available capacity; allocator logs show attach delays and slot fragmentation. NVMe IO queues show short high-amplitude bursts coincident with optimizer jobs.
- Expected: autoscaler should allocate/attach GPUs to meet demand without the attach delay cliff seen.

Initial temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Route critical traffic to a fallback model variant pinned to a different dedicated cluster or use hosted API fallback for high-importance endpoints while we investigate.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In a prod-like dedicated pool, schedule the background optimizer/prefetch-optimizer (service 'prefetch-opt') compaction with default concurrency during midday traffic spike.
2) Generate high fanout of short streaming requests (50-200ms per request typical) from a tenant pinned to the pool.
3) Monitor autoscaler, allocator attach latencies, and NVMe io util (iostat/pmem).
4) Observe transient nvme_io_wait spikes, kernel preemption logs, and delayed GPU attach leading to queuing and p99 latency spikes.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:05 - Ava Chen (Support): Notified Quillify that we are investigating. Asked for spike timing and sample request IDs. Customer provided sample req IDs: rq_7812,rq_7819.

2026-03-10 12:17 - Diego Morales (SRE): Correlated allocator attach_time with prefetch-opt compaction windows. Initial hypothesis: background optimizer is producing short NVMe bursts that cascade into kernel scheduling pressure and GPU attach latency.

2026-03-10 13:02 - Priya Nair (Runtime Eng): Looked at kernel traces. Found preempt_count spikes and nvme latency peaking at same timestamps. Suggested lowering prefetch-opt IO priority and limiting compaction concurrency as a quick mitigation.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Quillify (Customer): Applied fallback routing per Support's recommendation; reported partial relief for priority endpoints but general degradation persisted for bulk traffic. Asked for ETA on root cause and mitigation.

2026-03-11 15:20 - Diego Morales (SRE): Deployed temporary autoscaler weight change to decouple NVMe IO metric from immediate shrink decisions. Observed reduction in attach time spikes during next window.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Runtime Eng (Priya): Opened PR to add I/O niceness to prefetch-opt and to add a soft backoff to compaction when allocator attach latency rises (see related PR).
investigation_notes: Telemetry correlation: NVMe io wait bursts line up within +/-200ms of attach_timeout and kernel preemption logs across multiple nodes in dc-805.
Prefetch-opt behavior: compaction jobs run every 15 minutes by default; concurrency=8 produced highest observed IO envelope. Lowering concurrency to 2 reduced nvme spikes by ~70% in test cluster.

Autoscaler decisioning: autoscaler was using overall GPU utilization and not NVMe IO signals for short-term scale decisions; allocator was thrashing due to attach delays even though logical capacity existed.

Hypothesis: background compaction creates short-lived IO bursts that lead to kernel-level scheduling preemption and cause critical threads in the GPU attach path to be delayed, resulting in slot fragmentation and queuing at the allocator layer. This is a noisy-neighbor type interaction but driven by infra-service IO behavior rather than tenant compute alone.
Customer impact estimate: ~20-35% throughput loss over the affected 40-50 minute window; increased request latencies for short streams; some host-level 429s/attach_timeouts observed.
resolution_notes: - Reduced prefetch-opt concurrency on dc-805 from 8 to 2 during peak hours (immediate partial relief).
- Adjusted autoscaler weighting to make short-term NVMe io spikes less likely to trigger slot reclamation/shrink operations.
- Recommended customer route high-priority endpoints to a fallback cluster while fix rolled out.
- Merge PR to run prefetch-opt compaction under I/O niceness (ionice) and add adaptive backoff when allocator attach latency > 500ms (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3021).
- Update the ops playbook to schedule heavy compaction windows outside customer peak windows or to perform compactions at lower concurrency for dedicated pools.
- Add an autoscaler signal that directly monitors allocator attach latency and NVMe io microbursts to avoid oscillatory behaviour.
Status: mitigations in place; monitoring configured to watch next three midday windows. Work on PR in review. Customer notified and monitoring dashboard shared.
next_steps: 1) Runtime Eng to land PR adding ionice + backoff (owner: Priya Nair) - target: 2026-03-15.
2) Ops to add prefetch-opt concurrency tuning to dedicated pool runbook and to update maintenance scheduling UI to allow per-customer quiet windows (owner: Diego Morales) - target: 2026-03-20.
3) Telemetry team to build short-window NVMe microburst alerting and autoscaler integration test (owner: Mateo Ruiz) - target: 2026-03-22.
4) Follow-up call with Quillify to confirm resolution and remove fallback routing once two clean midday windows observed (owner: Ava Chen) - target: after PR merge and one-week validation.
5) Link this incident into postmortem board and add ops playbook snippet (owner: SRE) - target: 2026-03-25.
